message.content:
Below are two ways to spin‑up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You need the **GPU quota** for the zone you choose (e.g., `us-central1-a`).  
> * The **GPU driver package** will be installed automatically if you use the `--metadata` flag shown below.

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI Command

```bash
# Replace PROJECT_ID, ZONE, INSTANCE_NAME as needed
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
    --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata="install-nvidia-driver=true" \
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
```

### What this does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-project` / `--image-family` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Terminates the VM during host maintenance (recommended for GPU workloads). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the VM crashes. |
| `--metadata install-nvidia-driver=true` | Installs the NVIDIA driver automatically. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access (needed for driver installation). |

> 📌 **Tip** – If you prefer a different machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-16`), just change the `--machine-type` flag.

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine endpoint:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true" }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  }
}
```

### How to POST

```bash
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> ⚙️ **Authentication** – The `Authorization` header uses an OAuth 2.0 token obtained via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`.  
> 📁 **File** – Save the JSON above as `instance.json` and reference it with `@instance.json`.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Enable Compute Engine API |
| ✅ | Verify GPU quota for your zone |
| ✅ | Choose machine type (CPU/RAM) |
| ✅ | Set `--metadata install-nvidia-driver=true` (or metadata item in JSON) |
| ✅ | Use `--maintenance-policy TERMINATE` for GPU safety |
| ✅ | Grant `cloud-platform` scope (or `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`) |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with the correct driver version.

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
